question: What is the newly declared age for minors to operate bank accounts independently, as per the Reserve Bank of India’s recent guidelines?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 years.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed minors above the age of 10 years to independently operate savings/term deposit accounts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Minors aged 10 years and above can now open and operate savings or term deposit accounts independently, according to RBI's new guidelines.
 
• Banks are required to ensure that minor accounts are not overdrawn and always maintain a credit balance.
 
• Additional facilities like internet banking, debit cards, and cheque books may be offered based on the bank’s risk management policy.
 
• The new guidelines will be effective by July 1, 2025, and banks must amend their policies to align with the updated rules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **​Agency Overview:**
 
 
• Jurisdiction: Government of India

• **Functions:**
 
 
• Responsible for regulating the Indian banking system and currency
 
• Manages the supply and issuance of the Indian Rupee
 
• Promotes economic development
 
• Works on regulating payment systems through National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)
 
• Prints and mints Indian currency notes through Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran (BRBNM) division
 
• Provides deposit insurance and credit guarantees through the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)
 
 
 
• **Historical Facts:**
 
 
• Commenced operations on 1 April 1935, as per the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
 
• Nationalized on 1 January 1949, post India’s independence
 
 
 
• **Leadership Structure: **Direction of RBI is managed by a 21-member central board of directors, including:
 
 
• Governor
 
• Four Deputy Governors
 
• Two representatives from the Ministry of Finance
 
• Ten government-nominated directors
 
• Four directors from local boards in Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, and Delhi, each with five members representing regional interests
